To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical exponents and critical amplitudes of the Gross- Neveu model with 4 fermion interactions are in agreement with the results of a recent lattice simulation, that the critical behavior of the Gross- Neuveu model and the corresponding Neveu-Yakawa model are identical, and that the critical ex- ponents are in agreement with those of the O(N) model in d=3.

(1) the phase transition of the GN model with N fermion flavors is of second order in d=3, (2) it belongs to the universality class of the XY model in d=2, (3) the critical exponents are independent of N, (4) the scaling amplitudes depend on N.
the phase transition of the GN-model is of second order for all N and that the critical exponents and amplitudes depend on N.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the phase diagram of the 3-dimensional Gross-NeveU model.
the phase transition of the 2-dimensional Ising model in an external magnetic field.
the nonperturbative study of the phase transition of the N -component Gross-NeveU model in d = 4 - e dimensions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Gross-Neuveu model with N=2 fermion flavors is in the universality class of the 3d Ising model, and that the critical exponents of the N-flavor model are in the scaling regime with a critical exponent beta = 0.325(3) for N = 4 and beta = 0.
, for d = 3, the Gross-Neueu model with N = 1 and 2 fermions belongs to the same critical universality class as a free massless boson.
the critical exponents and the critical scaling functions of the Gross- Neveu model are in agreement with the predictions of the renormalization group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gross-Neueu model with N = 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 is in the same universality classes, while for N = 5 the critical exponents are slightly different.
the Gross-Neueu model is an excellent example for a nonperturbatively renormalizable field theory in the sense of Polchinski.
the effective average action is a powerful tool to investigate the critical behavior of strongly interacting fermions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effective average action can provide a powerful tool for studying the critical properties of field theories.
the effective average action is a very powerful tool to calculate critical exponents in the framework of the nonperturbative renormalization group.
the effective average action is an efficient tool to calculate critical exponents and amplitudes in the Gross-Neueu and the Neveu- Yukawa models.
